quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: Say "road" slowly and isolate just the target consonant. To make /r/, you curl your tongue tip back slightly without letting it touch the roof of your mouth. To make /w/, you round your lips into a small circle and glide, like starting to say "oo". Which one are you actually doing?
quests.explanation: The word "road" contains /r/, a voiced alveolar approximant, made by curling your tongue tip back slightly without letting it touch the roof of your mouth. It's easy to confuse with /w/, a voiced labial-velar approximant, but the two are produced quite differently.
quests.mouthPosition: Curl your tongue tip back slightly without letting it touch the roof of your mouth.

quests.explanation: "roar" is a good example of /r/: you curl your tongue tip back slightly without letting it touch the roof of your mouth. Compare that with /w/, where you'd instead round your lips into a small circle and glide, like starting to say "oo" — the two shouldn't be mixed up once you feel the difference.
quests.mouthPosition: To produce this sound, curl your tongue tip back slightly without letting it touch the roof of your mouth.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD

To produce /dʒ/, you stop the air just behind your top teeth, then release it as a hiss, with your voice on; /j/ is made differently, by raising the middle of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth and gliding, like starting to say "ee".
